== Security
The parser reads sources nobody vetted: a cloned example opened in the TUI, documentation, a project an AI agent
@@ -841,6 +841,15 @@ failures of the route go. A highlighted path that steps into an `onException` cl
The `<camel-topology-diagram>` web component no longer draws the error paths of the route topology as calls between
routes. With its new `errors` attribute it draws the routes reached only on error in a frame below the other routes.
+=== camel-jbang - route-diagram, route-structure and route-topology read Java sources without compiling them
+Given Java source files, `camel cmd route-diagram`, `camel cmd route-structure` and `camel cmd route-topology` (and the
+`camel_render_route_diagram` MCP tool) now read the routes with the Java DSL parser, as `camel transform route` and
+`camel overview` do, instead of compiling the sources and loading their routes in a short-lived Camel. A step the parser
+cannot work out, such as a lambda or a processor, is shown as a placeholder, and the parts it could not read are
+listed (with `--json`, as an `unread` array in the JSON). Use the new `--compile` option to compile the sources and
+load their routes as before.
=== camel-jbang - export to Quarkus keeps the names in `quarkus.*` keys
`camel export --runtime=quarkus` wrote every `quarkus.*` key except `quarkus.hawtio.*` in dash case: an upper-case

-Give a source file instead of a running integration to see the structure without running it.
+Give a source file instead of a running integration to see the structure without running it. A Java source file is read
+by the Java DSL parser, without compiling it; use `--compile` to compile it instead.
`--brief` shortens each node, and `--description` shows the description of each node instead of its code.

| `--box-width` | Node box width in logical pixels | 180 | int

| `--filter` | Filter route by filename or route id |  | String
| `--font-size` | Font size in logical pixels for node text | 12 | int
@@ -20,6 +20,7 @@ camel cmd route-structure [options]

| `--description` | To show description instead of code |  | boolean
| `--filter` | Filter route by filename or route id (multiple names can be separated by comma) |  | String

@@ -20,6 +20,7 @@ camel cmd route-topology [options]

| `--description` | Prefer route description over route id in node labels |  | boolean
| `--errors` | Draw the error handling: the routes reached only on error in a frame of their own below the routes, with where their failures come from (with --theme) |  | boolean
| `--external` | Include external systems (consumers at top, producers at bottom) |  | boolean
@@ -27,6 +27,11 @@ It also works with Java source files:
camel cmd route-diagram MyRoute.java
+Java routes are read by the Java DSL parser, without compiling them, so the diagram is ready in milliseconds and the
+source does not need its dependencies. A step the parser cannot work out, such as a lambda or a processor, is shown as a
+placeholder, and the parts it could not read are listed. Use `--compile` to compile the source and load its routes
+instead. The same applies to `camel cmd route-topology` and `camel cmd route-structure`.
